policy_name: Vendor Gifts, Hospitality, and Entertainment Policy
description: Gifts, hospitality, or entertainment given to or received from a vendor require pre-approval before the spend is incurred. Any gift, hospitality, or entertainment involving a government official requires pre-approval regardless of amount, reflecting the elevated bribery risk and criminal liability attached to public-official corruption.

policy_references.notes: Repealed the Prevention of Corruption Act, Cap. 144 and the Prevention of Corruption Act, 2012-31. Prohibits offering, promising, or granting a gift, money, or other advantage to a government official in connection with the performance of official duties, and extends corporate liability to companies and their directors/officers. Per a Lex Mundi anti-corruption compliance guide summary, its scope covers both public officials and private-sector counterparties. Penalties run up to BBD$1,500,000 or 15 years imprisonment on indictment. Does not specify a numeric gift-value threshold, so standard_approval_threshold and government_official_approval_threshold remain internal-policy values.

policy_references.citation: Internal Gifts, Hospitality, and Entertainment Standard
policy_references.notes: Sets standard_approval_threshold (150) and government_official_approval_threshold (0, i.e. any amount requires pre-approval when the counterparty is a government official).
